dateOverrides are not filtered to the availability user or schedule being evaluated, allowing one host's override to affect another host's slots.

goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

adjudication_records.issue_text: A slot within a date override returns available before busy intervals are checked, so calendar bookings inside the override can be offered as available.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the checkIfIsAvailable function in slots.ts, when a dateOverrideExist is true and the slot is within the override bounds, the function returns true at line 130 (after the dateOverrideExist check) WITHOUT checking the busy intervals. The busy.every() check at the end of the function is only reached if no date override exists or if the slot is outside the override. This means calendar bookings (busy times) within a date override period will be ignored, potentially double-booking slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dateOverrides are not filtered to the availability user or schedule being evaluated, allowing one host's override to affect another host's slots.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in checkIfIsAvailable function (lines 99-147), dateOverrides are passed as a parameter and checked against the slot time. However, examining how dateOverrides is constructed (lines 408-413), it includes all users' overrides with userId and timeZone. In the checkIfIsAvailable function, there's no filtering by userId - it checks ALL dateOverrides against the slot regardless of which user they belong to. This means if user A has a date override, it could incorrectly affect availability calculations for user B's slots. The workingHours check also doesn't filter by user. This is a real bug where one host's availability override could affect another host's slot availability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The override check accepts slots that start within an override but end after date.end, allowing bookings beyond overridden availability.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the checkIfIsAvailable function in slots.ts, the date override check logic (lines 99-130) checks if slotEndTime is before or same as date.start, or if slotStartTime is after date.end. However, it does NOT check if slotEndTime extends beyond date.end. The condition `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))` only checks if the slot starts after the override ends, but a slot that starts within the override window but ends after date.end would pass through and be considered available. This is a boundary condition bug where slots overlapping the end of an override period are incorrectly allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Working-hours validation rejects a slot when it is outside any matching working-hours range; split availability can therefore reject otherwise valid slots.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the working hours validation logic added in checkIfIsAvailable (lines 133-147), the code uses `workingHours.find()` which returns true if ANY working hour entry fails the bounds check. The condition `if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime)` returns true (marking slot as outside working hours) when the slot doesn't fit within a single working hour range. For split availability (e.g., 9-12 and 14-17), a slot at 10:00 would be checked against both ranges - it would fail the 14-17 range check (10:00 < 14:00) and thus be incorrectly rejected, even though it's valid within the 9-12 range. The logic should use `every()` to ensure the slot is outside ALL working hour ranges before rejecting, not `find()` which rejects if outside ANY single range.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Working-hours validation calculates end from the slot start rather than slotEndTime, so events extending past working hours can be considered valid.
